predictions.reasoning: A shift in the implied probability of Josh Shapiro winning the 2028 Democratic nomination has essentially no identifiable transmission channel to broad US equities over a 12-hour window. The event is roughly three years away, the nomination is contingent on a primary that has not begun, and there is no policy specificity attached to Shapiro versus other Democrats that would repriced any liquid asset now. Any move in this thin prediction market is far more likely to reflect intra-market noise, low liquidity, or personality-driven speculation than leaked information affecting cash-flow expectations of listed companies. The honest mapping is null.

llm_justification.summary: This market asks about the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination for Josh Shapiro, an event roughly three years out with no committed policy platform and no clear transmission channel to any liquid public-market instrument within a 12-hour window. The most defensible mapping is essentially null: any move in this thin market is more plausibly noise than actionable leaked information. We flag broad US equities only to state explicitly that no tradable signal exists here (expected move well below the 700bps threshold, very low confidence).
key_assumptions: The nomination remains distant and contingent, with no near-term binding market catalyst
No specific, market-moving policy is uniquely attached to Shapiro
Broad equity indices are insensitive to distant primary probability shifts
failure_modes: The mapping is genuinely null — treating any prediction-market move as informative would manufacture a false signal
The move could reflect a real, public event (announcement/scandal) already priced, offering no edge
Even if a real catalyst exists, the chosen equity proxy is only weakly (essentially not) exposed to it on this horizon
Reversal: thin-market probability spikes routinely mean-revert without any asset impact
